Zid's terms (zid.sa/ar/legal/terms-conditions/, held copies in the 20261027T112044Z-zid-rerender run and in other-product-class's 20261028T190806Z WARC), section on compensation in the Direct Shipping service (الشحن المباشر). The merchant raises a support ticket in the store dashboard (طلبات وبلاغات نظام تشغيل الشحن المباشر), for a damaged shipment within 24 hours or a lost one within 20 working days. For a lost shipment Zid contacts the carrier and traces it within 10 working days. If it is not found, "تنتقل زد إلى مرحلة المطالبة بالتعويض من شركة الشحن", but the decision and amount are the carrier's, "وليس لزد سيطرة". Compensation goes to the merchant's wallet within 30 working days. Placement own-service: Zid's shipping service takes the complaint and escalates it; the ticket sits in Zid's dashboard (core); the decision is outside (the carrier's). Condition: shipments of Zid's Direct Shipping service; the time limits and documents above.
why: The terms put the merchant's complaint about a carrier of Zid's Direct Shipping service in a support ticket in the store's own dashboard (the lines before the quote: طلبات وبلاغات نظام تشغيل الشحن المباشر), and Zid escalates it, claiming compensation from the carrier. So core, the strongest placement, holds. The decision on the claim and its amount is the carrier's, outside, as claimed. Nuance: the quoted escalation is done by Zid's own shipping service ("خدمة الشحن المباشر", its team), which reads more exactly as own-service. That would still establish the capability, so the count does not change. The claim says rightly that no statement shows carrier ratings.

True, as the claim says: no held location (AE, EG, GB, JP, OM, SA, US, YE) puts a suggestion in it; every suggestion is psp. But "an empty category shows the topic only" is a convention the source does not state. Scope OM is right for the line, and the same category is defined for all eight locations. Neither placement establishes the capability, so no count changes.

"Scope grants and limits a program's ability to read and write data" (held copy, 20261012T0419Z run, lines 188-190). [3] "Webhooks are accessible from the default scope that is automatically accessible to all API accounts." Placement core. Conditions: [2] app-level API accounts only; [1] a store-level account's scopes are fixed once made. App-level tokens come after a store owner or authorised user installs and authorises the app.
why: The three sentences are BigCommerce's own API documentation of its OAuth scopes: store-level scopes fixed once made, the app-level-only scope store_app_extensions_manage, and the default scope open to all API accounts. That is the platform's own access-scope system, core, as claimed. The quotes are in the held copy as cited. The app-level account requirement is a kind of API account, not a scope the definitions name, and line [2] records it, so the empty scope is right.
